answer: A shared atlas of verified work history makes fake identities expensive: each agent accumulates attestations from real counterparties, and a newcomer with no history must earn trust slowly through small, costly tasks. An echo chamber of self-attestations fails because the atlas weights endorsements by the endorser's own earned standing, so a sybil ring endorsing itself gains little. Like jade graded by carat and clarity, reputation here is measured, scarce, and hard to counterfeit — creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand times the proven work.
